findings.title: entities.py's A3 orjson checks are red or green by whether the optional, unpinned orjson is installed
findings.claim: tests/entities.py, a script in the measured production closure of all 64 production modules, reports 3 of 1678 checks failed on the pristine baseline tree whenever the optional, unpinned package orjson is importable, because tests/hastub's json_bytes stub takes an orjson.dumps fast path that does not refuse non-finite floats and its refusal walk() is only reached when orjson is missing.
findings.mechanism: tests/hastub/homeassistant/helpers/__init__.py:_json_bytes returns orjson.dumps(obj) inside a try/except ImportError. orjson.dumps serialises float('inf') instead of refusing it, so the hand-written walk() below -- the code the docstring calls 'orjson's refusals' -- is dead on any box where orjson is installed. tests/entities.py asserts json_bytes({'k': inf}) raises, so three A3 checks fail. tests/requirements-ci.txt does not pin orjson.

evidence.unit: failing checks of 1678 in tests/entities.py on the pristine baseline tree
evidence.machine: 8-core Apple M1, 8 GB, macOS 25.6.0, Python 3.11 (framework), numpy 2.4.6 / scipy 1.17.1
evidence.contention_note: shared audit box, load1 5.5-12.3 during the fan-out; every wall and CPU number here is provisional and the quiet window re-takes it

perturbation.change: make 'import orjson' fail (sys.modules['orjson'] = None), which is the shape of a runner that has not installed it
perturbation.observed_value: 3 -> 0 failing checks; json_bytes({'k': inf}) moves accepted -> refused (ValueError)

findings.metric_definition: R.check failures tests/entities.py prints in its own closing line, on the unmutated baseline tree

null_control.command: PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/entities.py ; then the same with sys.modules['orjson'] = None
null_control.value: 3 of 1678 ENTITY CHECKS FAILED (exit 1) / ALL 1678 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED (exit 0)
null_control.note: Both arms are a pristine baseline tree; only the importability of orjson differs, so the effect is not the tree.

reproduction_steps: python3 -c "import sys,os,runpy; sys.path.insert(0,os.path.abspath('tests')); sys.modules['orjson']=None; runpy.run_path('tests/entities.py', run_name='__main__')"   # ALL 1678 PASSED
findings.proposed_fix_scope: tests/hastub/homeassistant/helpers/__init__.py -- run the non-finite/set/bytes walk before the orjson fast path, or give the fast path the same refusals. One file; no production code, no version bump.

non_findings.claim: entities.py's three reds are an instrument defect, not a production defect: the chain is entirely inside tests/hastub
non_findings.value: json_bytes({'k': inf}) accepted as found, refused with orjson blocked; production is untouched by the perturbation
